domain_note: Authenticated bytes are the ASCII domain, one NUL byte, then the canonical payload with signature or mac removed; canonical_hex is that preimage.
warning: Every secret and seed here is a published test value from the evidence-exchange/v2 corpora and must never sign anything real.
why_this_file_exists: Whether a verified artifact is applied, accepted with no change, refused restatement_conflict, or left undecided by a store fault depends on the records the receiver already holds, which no wire artifact can express. Each case states every held record before, the artifact, any injected store fault, the answer, and every held record after.
sealed_note: Receiver state shared by every case. chain_row_digest and envelope_digest are SHA-256 of the UTF-8 labels 'ori-specs evidence-exchange/v3 restated records chain row N' and '... envelope N', and each sealed checkpoint digest of '... checkpoint N'; they stand for the bytes the receiver sealed. A receipt's range_digest is taken over these chain_row_digest values.
material_note: The custody secrets are custody-acknowledgement.json's gateway_secret_hex and previous_gateway_secret_hex. The active receipt and epoch keys are delivery-receipt-v2.json's; the verify_only receipt and epoch keys are authority-key-registry-v2.json's test keys 0 and 3; the disposition key is evidence-disposition-v2.json's. The earlier epoch and its key are delivery-envelope.json's superseded_epoch case and previous_generation_seed_hex.
state_note: held_before and held_after carry exactly the members custody, receipts, epoch_confirmations, active_epoch, registration_obligations, dispositions, stops and application_storage_fault, as evidence-exchange/v3 Test vectors defines them.
answer_note: expected is accept (answered as applied), reject with reject_reason, or undecided (a store fault at any point but at_refusal_record: reject_reason and applied_sequences null). store_fault is null, at_read, after_first_write, at_commit or at_refusal_record, as evidence-exchange/v3 Test vectors defines them.

cases.name: custody_first_acceptance
cases.note: Nothing is held for local_seq 1. Not a restatement: custody is recorded with this acknowledgement's time and generation, and the receiver's record time.

cases.name: custody_identical_repeat
cases.note: Byte-identical to the acknowledgement whose custody is held. Agrees: accepted, and the custody record is unchanged.

cases.name: custody_same_time_previous_generation
cases.note: Custody was first recorded under the active generation; this names the same custody_at_ms under the verify_only generation. Agrees: the generation is not part of agreement, and the held key_id stays the first.

cases.name: custody_same_time_active_generation
cases.note: Custody was first recorded under the verify_only generation; this names the same custody_at_ms under the active one. Agrees, and the held key_id stays the verify_only generation's.

cases.name: custody_different_time_active_generation
cases.note: Names a custody_at_ms other than the held one, under the active generation. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and nothing is written.

cases.name: custody_different_time_previous_generation
cases.note: Names a custody_at_ms other than the held one, under the verify_only generation. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and nothing is written.

cases.name: custody_agreeing_fills_missing_record_time
cases.note: Custody is held without a record time, as a receiver that kept none recorded it. An agreeing restatement supplies the record time from the receiver's clock and nothing else.

cases.name: custody_conflicting_supplies_no_record_time
cases.note: Custody is held without a record time. A conflicting restatement is refused and supplies no record time.

cases.name: custody_store_fault_at_commit
cases.note: The store fails at commit while first recording custody for local_seq 1. Rolled back: nothing is held, the artifact is neither applied nor refused, and the application-storage fault signal is raised.

cases.name: custody_conflict_refusal_record_unwritable
cases.note: A restatement whose custody_at_ms conflicts with the held one. The refusal is decided, and then the store fails writing the record of that refusal. The refusal is still answered restatement_conflict, every held record is unchanged, and the failed write raises the signal.

cases.name: custody_store_fault_reading_held_record
cases.note: A restatement whose custody_at_ms conflicts with the held one, but the store fails reading the held custody record the decision needs. A read fault is a store fault even where the decision would have been a refusal: undecided, no rejection reason, nothing changes, and the signal is raised.

cases.name: custody_conflict_leaves_fault_signal_raised
cases.note: The fault signal is raised from an earlier fault. A refusal is not a successful application, so it stays raised.

cases.name: custody_agreeing_restatement_clears_fault_signal
cases.note: The fault signal is raised from an earlier fault. An agreeing restatement is answered as applied, and its application completes, so the signal clears.

cases.name: receipt_identical_repeat
cases.note: Identical to the receipt that applied 1..2. Every sequence is held: nothing is applied, it is answered as applied, and nothing changes.

cases.name: receipt_union_over_held_prefix
cases.note: 1 is receipted; this receipt covers 1..3 at a later accepted_at_ms. Not a conflict: 2 and 3 are applied with this receipt's time and key, and 1 keeps its first time.

cases.name: receipt_union_over_held_suffix
cases.note: 3 is receipted; this receipt covers 1..3 at a later accepted_at_ms. 1 and 2 are applied with this receipt's time and key, and 3 keeps its first time.

cases.name: receipt_union_over_sequences_receipted_under_another_key
cases.note: 1..2 were receipted under the receipt key the registry now holds verify_only; this receipt covers 1..3 under the active key. 3 takes the active key; 1 and 2 keep the verify_only key and their first time.

cases.name: receipt_store_fault_after_first_sequence_write
cases.note: The union over 1..3 applies 2 and 3. The store fails on the write after the first sequence it applies. Rolled back: no sequence of the range is written, the artifact is undecided, and the signal is raised.

cases.name: receipt_store_fault_while_signal_raised
cases.note: The signal is already raised from an earlier fault, and the store fails again at commit. Every store fault raises the signal whether or not it is raised: it stays raised, and nothing else changes.

cases.name: receipt_store_fault_at_commit
cases.note: The same union, with the store failing at commit. Rolled back as above.

cases.name: receipt_redelivered_after_store_fault
cases.note: The receipt the faulted attempt left undecided, delivered again once the store recovers. Decided afresh: 2 and 3 are applied, and the signal clears.

cases.name: confirmation_identical
cases.note: Identical to the confirmation held for the current epoch. Agrees: accepted, and the confirmation record, the active-epoch projection, the obligation and the effective epoch are unchanged.

cases.name: confirmation_different_confirmed_at
cases.note: The current epoch is confirmed; this confirms it again at another confirmed_at_ms. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and no record of the epoch changes.

cases.name: confirmation_different_actor
cases.note: The current epoch is confirmed; this names another actor. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and no record of the epoch changes.

cases.name: confirmation_different_key_id
cases.note: The current epoch is confirmed under the active epoch key; this is signed under the verify_only epoch key, with the same actor and time. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and no record of the epoch changes.

cases.name: confirmation_earlier_epoch_agreeing_restatement
cases.note: Both epochs are confirmed and the current one is active and effective. This restates the earlier epoch's confirmation exactly. Agrees: accepted, every confirmation record, the projection, every obligation and the effective epoch are unchanged; the projection does not move to the earlier epoch.

cases.name: confirmation_earlier_epoch_conflicting_restatement
cases.note: Both epochs are confirmed and the current one is active and effective. This restates the earlier epoch's confirmation with another actor. Conflicts: refused restatement_conflict, and no record of any epoch changes.

cases.name: confirmation_for_another_epoch
cases.note: An earlier epoch is confirmed and effective; the current epoch, the one the receiver seals under, is open. Not a restatement: its confirmation is recorded, the projection and the effective epoch move to it, and its obligation closes.

cases.name: confirmation_store_fault_after_first_write
cases.note: As confirmation_for_another_epoch, with the store failing on the write after the confirmation record. Rolled back: the confirmation record, the projection, the obligation and the effective epoch are as before, and the signal is raised.

cases.name: confirmation_store_fault_at_commit
cases.note: As confirmation_for_another_epoch, with the store failing at commit. Rolled back as above.

cases.name: confirmation_conflict_leaves_fault_signal_raised
cases.note: A conflicting confirmation while the signal is raised. Refused, and the signal stays raised.

cases.name: disposition_first_application
cases.note: An epoch-scoped epoch_reprovisioning_required for the current epoch, triggered by a sealed checkpoint. Applied: the disposition and its epoch stop are recorded.

cases.name: disposition_byte_identical_repeat
cases.note: Byte-identical to the applied disposition. v2's rule: applied again with no new state.

cases.name: disposition_no_new_effect_is_superseded
cases.note: Another epoch-scoped disposition for the current epoch, triggered by another sealed checkpoint, while that epoch's stop is in force. v2's rule: refused superseded, never restatement_conflict; nothing changes.

cases.name: disposition_epoch_under_identity_stop_same_epoch
cases.note: An identity stop is in force. An epoch-scoped disposition for the current epoch has no new effect, since the identity stop already covers every epoch: refused superseded, and nothing changes.

cases.name: disposition_epoch_under_identity_stop_other_epoch
cases.note: An identity stop is in force. An epoch-scoped disposition for the earlier epoch, triggered by a checkpoint sealed under it, is likewise covered: refused superseded, and nothing changes.

cases.name: disposition_identity_under_epoch_stop
cases.note: An epoch stop for the current epoch is in force. An identity-scoped disposition has a new effect, stopping every other epoch too: applied, and an identity stop is added beside the epoch stop, which stays.

cases.name: disposition_identity_byte_identical_repeat
cases.note: Byte-identical to the applied identity disposition. v2's rule: applied again with no new state.

cases.name: disposition_artifact_scope_under_identity_stop
cases.note: An identity stop is in force. An artifact-scoped artifact_terminal on a sealed checkpoint is not an epoch or identity disposition, so step 6 does not supersede it: applied, its record is added, no stop is added, and the identity stop is unchanged.

cases.name: disposition_resigned_body_under_its_stop
cases.note: The same body as the applied epoch disposition under another valid signature. A different signature makes a different artifact, so it is not a byte-identical repeat, and its stop is in force: refused superseded, and nothing changes.

cases.name: disposition_resigned_artifact_scope_body
cases.note: The same body as an applied artifact-scoped disposition under another valid signature. It is a different artifact and no stop decides it: applied as a new disposition, with its own record and artifact_digest beside the first.

cases.name: disposition_store_fault_after_first_write
cases.note: As disposition_first_application, with the store failing on the write after the disposition record. Rolled back: no disposition and no stop is held, the artifact is undecided, and the signal is raised.

cases.name: disposition_store_fault_at_commit
cases.note: As disposition_first_application, with the store failing at commit. Rolled back as above.

cases.name: disposition_redelivered_after_store_fault
cases.note: The disposition the faulted attempt left undecided, delivered again. Nothing of the faulted attempt is held, so it is not a repetition under v2's rule: it is applied as a first application, and the signal clears.
